case_title: Mohan Singh v. State of Bihar
trial_court_outcome: Convicted for conspiracy of murder and extortion of money
neutral_facts: The accused, Mohan Singh, was involved in a series of telephone calls with the informant, Vikas Kumar Jha, demanding Rs.50,000/- and threatening dire consequences if the demand was not met. On the day of the incident, the informant received a call from his driver stating that his brother and father had been shot at their medical store. The brother died, and the father was injured. The informant identified the voice of the caller as that of the accused. The trial court convicted the accused for conspiracy to commit murder and extortion. The High Court upheld the conviction, finding that the evidence of the informant and the investigating officers supported the conclusion that the accused was guilty. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, affirming the conviction for life imprisonment under Section 120-B of the IPC for the murder of the victim.
